claims.text: Localized friction stir processing of damaged CoCrFeMnNi induces dynamic recrystallization and grain refinement.
Friction stir processing can heal preexisting cracks in CoCrFeMnNi.
Friction stir processing eliminates the hot-cracking risk associated with fusion-welding repair.
The target CoCrFeMnNi or similar high-entropy-alloy component exhibits microcracks, high residual stresses, and susceptibility to fusion-welding hot cracking.
FSP uses a rotating, traversing tool to generate frictional heat, plasticization, and substantial deformation in the processed region.
The proposed FSP repair is performed in an inert atmosphere.
The proposed FSP repair thermomechanically reworks CoCrFeMnNi without reaching its melting temperature.
Rotational speeds of 800–1000 rpm and traverse speeds of 50–70 mm/min are suitable boundaries for the proposed repair.
The proposed parameters keep the peak repair temperature below 0.6 times the melting temperature.
Post-repair performance is relevant from room temperature through 1000 °C under simulated aggressive service conditions.
Dynamic recrystallization and grain refinement reduce residual stresses in the stir zone.
Dynamic recrystallization and grain refinement eliminate preexisting microcracks and deleterious phase segregation.
Solid-state plastic deformation and frictional heating during FSP promote dynamic recrystallization without melting.
FSP creates an ultrafine-grained, homogenized repair zone and avoids brittle intermetallic phases typical of fusion-welded joints.
Compared with traditional fusion-welding repair, FSP produces a crack-free microstructure with greater ductility and high-temperature strength.
The improved FSP repair zone extends component service life under aggressive operating conditions.
Traditional fusion-welding repair is prone to hot cracking and undesirable phase formation due to remelting.
Variability in local material conditions can affect FSP repair quality and reproducibility.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field includes CoCrFeMnNi or a similar high-entropy alloy, whereas the boundary restricts applicability specifically to CoCrFeMnNi components.
